ApplicationIn.description:
Setting up a practitioner profile.

Short on purpose. This was an essay — where you trained, and a written
sample reading — which is a reasonable thing to ask a stranger and a
terrible thing to put between someone and joining. What a reader actually
chooses on is the name, the photograph, the languages and what you practise;
everything else can be filled in later from the desk.
ApplicationIn.title: ApplicationIn

ApplicationOut.description:
What an applicant sees about their own application.

Carries back everything they submitted, so the waiting page can show the
profile they made rather than a single line saying it is with a reviewer.

`reviewer_note` is deliberately absent. It is the reviewer's working
notes — "references did not respond", "second opinion needed" — and
`decision_note` is the message written to be read.
ApplicationOut.title: ApplicationOut

ApplicationReviewOut.description: The same application, as a reviewer sees it. Admin routes only.
ApplicationReviewOut.title: ApplicationReviewOut

AvakhadaOut.description:
Traditional birth attributes, all derived from the Moon.

`paya` is deliberately absent: the rules in circulation disagree and give
different metals for the same chart, so the engine declines to invent one.

name_syllable.description: Syllable traditionally used to name the child
name_syllable.title: Name Syllable

AvakhadaOut.title: AvakhadaOut

siddhanta.description: Which system computes the Sun and Moon, and therefore the panchang, the dashas and the avakhada. `surya` is सूर्य सिद्धान्त, what a Nepali kundali is cast from, and the default. `drik` is the modern ephemeris — better astronomy, and what AstroSage and AstroTalk publish, so use it to compare against those. The five star-planets are drik either way.
siddhanta.title: Siddhanta

tz_name.description: IANA zone name. NOT a UTC offset: the offset for a place changes over time, and sending a fixed one silently corrupts historical charts.
tz_name.title: Tz Name

BoundaryWarningOut.description:
A panchanga element close to changing.

Present because a traditional Nepali almanac's Moon runs 10-20 arcminutes
ahead of a modern ephemeris, which matters only near a boundary — and
there it decides the nakshatra, and with it the dasha lord and the name
syllable. A reading that says "Magha" flatly when Purva Phalguni is nine
minutes away is claiming more than the arithmetic supports.

minutes.description: Minutes from the birth moment until it changes.
minutes.title: Minutes

upcoming.description: What it becomes when it changes.
upcoming.title: Upcoming

BoundaryWarningOut.title: BoundaryWarningOut

engine_version.description: Bumped whenever a calculation rule changes. Surfacing it makes 'why did my chart change?' answerable.
engine_version.title: Engine Version

siddhanta.description: Which system the positions come from. Drik (दृक् सिद्धान्त) is modern and observational; most hand-cast Nepali panchangas follow सूर्य सिद्धान्त, whose Moon runs roughly a quarter degree ahead. That only changes anything near a boundary — see `panchang.near_boundary`.
siddhanta.title: Siddhanta

tribhagi.description: Vimshottari with a third removed — an 80-year cycle.

yogini.description: The eight yoginis over 36 years. `birth_lord` and each period's `lord` name a yogini, not a graha.

messages.description: Conversation so far. Only the most recent turns are sent to the model.
messages.title: Messages

milan.description: A finished Ashtakoota match, when the consultation was opened from one. Additive: absent for every single-chart session.

astrological_basis.description: Short tag naming the placement the answer rests on, e.g. '10th House Virgo · Exalted Mercury in D1'.
astrological_basis.title: Astrological Basis

highlight_house.description: House for the client to highlight in the chart, if the answer is about one. Null when no single house is implicated.
highlight_house.title: Highlight House

messages.description: Always empty in the session *list* — loading every message body for every session made that endpoint one query per session. Fetch a single session to get its messages.
messages.title: Messages

ChatTurn.description: One prior turn, as the client already stores it.
ChatTurn.title: ChatTurn

bhabhoga_ghati.description: भभोग — ghatis the Moon takes to cross the whole nakshatra. The balance is the lord's years times (1 - bhukta/bhabhoga).
bhabhoga_ghati.title: Bhabhoga Ghati

bhukta_ghati.description: भुक्त — ghatis of the janma nakshatra already elapsed at birth. Every Nepali kundali prints this beside the balance.
bhukta_ghati.title: Bhukta Ghati

ends_at.description: Local time the element gives way to the next.
ends_at.title: Ends At

GoogleSignInIn.description:
One Google sign-in, arriving by either of the two flows Google offers.

`code` is the web client's: a popup auth-code flow, which is the only way
to start sign-in from a button we designed ourselves. `credential` is an
ID token handed straight to the page, which is what a native mobile Google
Sign-In returns. Both end at the same verified identity.
GoogleSignInIn.title: GoogleSignInIn

sign_index.description: 0-11, Aries=0. The traditional North Indian chart prints the rashi number (sign_index + 1) in each house.
sign_index.title: Sign Index

MilanAnalysisRequest.description:
Birth details, not a finished match.

The match is recomputed server-side so the model can only ever read a score
the engine produced — and so the request stays four fields wide instead of
carrying two full charts back up the wire.
MilanAnalysisRequest.title: MilanAnalysisRequest

MilanContextIn.description:
A finished match, handed to the model as data.

Present only when the visitor opened the consultation from a milan
result. Every figure was computed by `astrology_core.milan`; the model
reads it and never recomputes it.
MilanContextIn.title: MilanContextIn

MilanKutaBrief.description: One koota's score, as the engine computed it.
MilanKutaBrief.title: MilanKutaBrief

masa.description: Solar month by the Sun's sidereal sign — Bhadra when it is in Leo. These are the Bikram Sambat month names.
masa.title: Masa

ritu.description: Season: two solar months to each of six.

samvatsara.description: Name of the year in the sixty-year Jovian cycle, e.g. Vibhava.

vara.description: Weekday by Vedic reckoning: the day turns at sunrise, so a pre-dawn birth belongs to the previous weekday.
vara.title: Vara

PractitionerCard.description:
One row of the directory.

Rating and consultation count are absent until reviews exist — a card that
invents `4.9 · 1,204 readings` for someone who has taken no consultations
is a fabricated credential, and the preview data in the web app is already
labelled as such for the same reason.
PractitionerCard.title: PractitionerCard

PractitionerStats.description:
What a reader needs to judge somebody, and nothing invented.

Every figure is counted from rows that exist. A practitioner with no
consultations has zeroes and a `rating_average` of None — not 4.9, and not
a hidden section that makes the page look complete.
PractitionerStats.title: PractitionerStats

ProfileIn.description:
What a practitioner may change about their own listing.

`verification_state` is not here. A practitioner cannot verify themselves.
ProfileIn.title: ProfileIn

ProfileUpdateIn.description:
What a person may change about themselves.

Not the email: it is the login identity and the key Google sign-in matches
on, so changing it is an account-recovery flow rather than a text field.
Not the role either — an account cannot promote itself.
ProfileUpdateIn.title: ProfileUpdateIn

A rate of zero withdraws that medium rather than making it free: the

info.description:
One backend, two clients (web and Flutter).

**Compatibility:** additive changes only within `/v1` — no removed or renamed
fields, no newly-required request fields, no narrowed types. App Store users
stay on old builds for months. Clients must treat unknown enum values as
"other". See docs/architecture.md §7.

**Errors** are always `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"}}`. Switch on
`code`; never parse `message`.
info.title: Nakhatra API

post.description:
Computes a full Vedic chart from birth details: Lahiri ayanamsa, whole-sign houses, mean nodes, Vimshottari dasha. Deterministic and synchronous — the calculation is local arithmetic against an ephemeris, not a job.

See docs/astrology-methodology.md for every methodology decision.

parameters.description: Dasha levels to return: 1 maha, 2 +antar, 3 +pratyantar. Defaults to 2 — the full tree is 819 periods and ~78KB, against ~12KB for two levels. Request 3 only when drilling into a specific period.

post.description: Recomputes the match from the same birth details and hands it, with both complete charts, to the model — which kootas matched and which did not, the outlook for the marriage, any dosha and what it bears on, and the remedies for it. Separate from `/match` because the arithmetic returns in milliseconds and the reading does not.
post.summary: A Jyotish reading of an Ashtakoota match

get.description:
A run of days with the panchang each one is read by.

The Bikram Sambat month is not computed here: it is a published table
rather than something the sky knows, and the client already owns it. This
serves whatever span of days the client asks for, and the client decides
which of them make up Bhadra.

Unauthenticated, like the rasifal — a calendar is public by nature.

Prefix search over 786,650 populated places. Every populated place in Nepal and India, plus everywhere worldwide with population >= 1000.

Alternate names are searched too — GeoNames records Lumbini under the primary name 'Rummin-dei', so searching primary names alone would make it unfindable.

Each result carries an **IANA zone name**, resolved here rather than guessed by the client.
Only verified, listed profiles are returned — the filter is in the query itself, not a caller's responsibility. Unauthenticated, because browsing is how someone decides whether to sign up.

post.summary: Apply to practise on the platform

get.description:
Serve a cached mp3.

Deliberately unauthenticated: the browser fetches this from an `<audio>` tag,
which sends no Authorization header. The name is a SHA-256 of the text, so it
is unguessable, and `cache.path_for` rejects anything that is not a name this
service could have written.
